propositions.text: The claimant is 26, Mexican citizen, claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97 for membership in homosexual social group

paragraphs.summary: The claimant, a 26-year-old Mexican, claims refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97 for being homosexual, alleging supporting facts.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges he is homosexual and his problems with his lover began in 2008

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he is homosexual and his problems with his lover began in 2008.

propositions.text: The claimant had a romantic relationship with XXXX since 2006

paragraphs.summary: The claimant had a romantic relationship with XXXX since 2006.

propositions.text: In March 2008, claimant met politician XXXX who showed interest and they started a secret affair a month later

paragraphs.summary: In March 2008, claimant met politician XXXX who showed interest and they started a secret affair a month later.

propositions.text: Claimant ended relationship with XXXX because he was ashamed of deceiving him
XXXX was offended and began harassing claimant, threatening to get rid of XXXX

paragraphs.summary: Claimant ended relationship with XXXX due to shame; XXXX was offended and harassed claimant, threatening to get rid of XXXX.

propositions.text: Claimant began noticing strange people near where he and XXXX lived

paragraphs.summary: Claimant began noticing strange people near where he and XXXX lived.

propositions.text: Claimant warned XXXX he would reveal evidence of their relationship if harassment continued

paragraphs.summary: Claimant warned XXXX he would reveal evidence of their relationship if harassment continued.

propositions.text: Police informed claimant that XXXX had been killed; claimant identified body
Claimant wanted to report threats but changed mind after police mocked him for saying XXXX was his lover

paragraphs.summary: Police informed claimant that XXXX was killed; claimant identified body but did not report threats due to police mockery.

propositions.text: Claimant lived with a friend; XXXX called to warn he knew claimant's location
Claimant sought refuge in city XXXXX but XXXX called again threatening to kill claimant if he refused to return

paragraphs.summary: Claimant lived with a friend; XXXX warned he knew claimant's location and threatened to kill him if he refused to return.

propositions.text: Claimant changed phone number and traveled to XXXXXXXX
XXXX called claimant again threatening to kill him within 24 hours

paragraphs.summary: Claimant changed phone number and traveled to XXXXXXXX; XXXX called again threatening to kill him within 24 hours.

propositions.text: Claimant left Mexico fearing for his life on XXXXX, 2008

paragraphs.summary: Claimant left Mexico fearing for his life on XXXXX, 2008.

propositions.text: Claimant claimed refugee protection in Montréal on June 27, 2008

paragraphs.summary: Claimant claimed refugee protection in Montréal on June 27, 2008.

propositions.text: After hearing testimony and evidence, claim cannot be allowed for stated reasons

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes the claim cannot be allowed after hearing testimony and evidence.

propositions.text: Claimant married XXXX in Montréal in 2010, establishing nexus with homosexual social group under section 96

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant married XXXX in Montréal in 2010, establishing nexus with homosexual social group under section 96.

propositions.text: Claimant's identity was established to panel's satisfaction with Mexican passport and CIC copies

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant's identity established with Mexican passport and CIC copies.

propositions.text: Claimant's testimony was not credible, with examples to follow

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant's testimony not credible, citing examples.

propositions.text: Claimant fears XXXX will kill him upon return to Mexico

paragraphs.summary: Claimant fears XXXX will kill him upon return to Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant testified XXXX is a well-known politician in XXXXX and belongs to party 'XXX'
Claimant said 'XXX' stands for XXXXXXXXXXX XXXXX and XXXX had XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX 2008

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified XXXX is a well-known politician in XXXXX belonging to party 'XXX' and gave party details.

propositions.text: No party called 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' found in evidence; 'XXX' is second-largest parliamentary group in Mexico

paragraphs.summary: The panel found no party called 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'; 'XXX' is second-largest parliamentary group in Mexico.

propositions.text: No evidence of politician named XXXXXXXXXX or that XXXX was XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX in 2008
Panel concludes XXXX is not part of Mexico's political scene, questioning claimant's story truthfulness

paragraphs.summary: The panel found no evidence of politician XXXXXXXXXX or XXXX's political role, questioning claimant's story truthfulness.

propositions.text: Claimant testified affair with XXXXX began and ended in 2008 by telephone
Claimant said XXXXX sometimes accompanied him to his door

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified his affair with XXXXX began and ended in 2008 and that XXXXX sometimes accompanied him to his door.

propositions.text: Claimant testified next face-to-face meeting with XXXXX was in 2008 at his workplace
Claimant testified XXXXX mentioned he was going to get rid of XXXXX on that date

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified his next meeting with XXXXX was in 2008 at work, where XXXXX said he would get rid of XXXXX.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he noticed strange people in a pickup truck outside his home in 2008
Claimant said these people were XXXXX employees and security staff
Claimant said six security officers usually accompanied them to meeting locations
Why claimant stated he started noticing strange people rather than recognizing security officers

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified about strange people outside his home who were XXXXX security staff, but was questioned about inconsistency in his narrative.

propositions.text: Claimant clearly alleged strangers outside his house, not that it was strange they were there
Claimant tried to brush aside inconsistency, which panel found flagrant
Reasonable to expect claimant to clearly disclose recognizing security officers if true
Inconsistency undermines claimant's credibility

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the claimant's inconsistency about strangers versus security officers flagrant and undermining his credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant initially testified telephone contact with XXXXX in 2008, then amended to no contact

paragraphs.summary: The claimant initially said he had telephone contact with XXXXX in 2008, then changed to no contact.

propositions.text: Claimant said he threatened to reveal cards, gifts, photos after XXXXX was killed
Why claimant stated he threatened XXXXX before murder in narrative
Claimant said he was stressed, confused events, threatened XXXXX on different date
Claimant's explanation does not satisfy the panel

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said he threatened XXXXX after murder but narrative said before; his explanation did not satisfy the panel.

propositions.text: Claimant should speak with consistency, integrity, accuracy about events causing fear

paragraphs.summary: The panel stated the claimant should speak consistently and accurately about events causing his fear.

propositions.text: Claimant sought refuge with friend and received threatening calls from XXXXX in 2008
Claimant changed phone number but XXXXX still called demanding photos or death threat

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified he fled to a friend's home and received threatening calls from XXXXX demanding photos.

propositions.text: Claimant said he told XXXXX he had photos but had deleted them
Why no mention of photos in narrative paragraph 15
Claimant answered 'I do not know' about missing photos mention
Claimant's explanation does not satisfy the panel

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said he deleted photos but did not mention them in narrative; his explanation did not satisfy the panel.

propositions.text: Claimant alleged XXXXX wanted to resume romantic relationship
Claimant alleged XXXXX killed XXXXX for that reason alone

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleged XXXXX wanted to resume relationship and killed XXXXX for that reason alone.

propositions.text: Claimant stated last threats were to kill in 24 hours
Claimant said XXXXX wanted incriminating photos
Claimant added new element to embellish claim and is not credible

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the claimant added new elements about photos to embellish his claim and is not credible.

propositions.text: Claimant said XXXXX was killed by gunshot
Claimant said newspaper reported murder as attempted theft
Why claimant did not submit newspaper article
Claimant said XXXXX name not mentioned and he did not keep article

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said XXXXX was shot and newspaper reported attempted theft; he did not submit article as name was missing.

propositions.text: Claimant submitted faxed email from 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' dated 2011 to corroborate murder
Panel attaches little probative value to this document

paragraphs.summary: The claimant submitted a 2011 faxed email to corroborate murder, but the panel gave it little probative value.

propositions.text: Rule 28(1) requires documents in English/French or with translation and translator's declaration

paragraphs.summary: Rule 28(1) requires documents be in English or French or have translation and translator's declaration.

propositions.text: No translator's declaration was provided as required by rule 28

paragraphs.summary: No translator's declaration was provided as required by rule 28.

propositions.text: Claimant said author of email was lawyer, 'friend of a friend'
Document lacks header, address, signature typical of law firms
No indication document is legal, probative, or relevant

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said email author was a lawyer friend, but document lacks typical legal features and probative value.

propositions.text: Document mentions deceased boyfriend and estate but no evidence murder as described

paragraphs.summary: The panel found no evidence in the document establishing murder as claimant described.

propositions.text: Claimant submitted another faxed email from a friend in Mexico dated 2011
Panel attaches little probative value to this document

paragraphs.summary: The claimant submitted another 2011 faxed email from a friend, which the panel gave little probative value.

propositions.text: No translator's declaration provided for second document as required by rule 28
Content is subjective and not from independent reliable source
Document produced solely to embellish refugee claim

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the second document lacked translation declaration, was subjective, and produced to embellish claim.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he had not travelled outside Mexico before Canada in 2008
Why passport issued five weeks before Canada travel
Claimant said planned Cuba vacation with XXXXX in July 2008
Panel concludes claimant intended to travel to Canada, not Cuba, and invented persecution story

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said he planned Cuba vacation but panel concluded he intended Canada travel and invented persecution story.

propositions.text: State is presumed capable of protecting citizens except in complete state breakdown situations
International protection applies only if claimant has no alternative to state protection

paragraphs.summary: The court states the presumption that states can protect citizens except in total breakdown, so international protection applies only if no alternative exists.

propositions.text: Claimant must prove on balance of probabilities that state protection is inadequate

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant must prove state protection is inadequate on a balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Did not file complaint with Mexican authorities due to XXXXX influence in Mexico
Claimant's assertion of XXXXX's influence insufficient to justify not seeking state protection

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges XXXXX's influence prevented complaint filing; the court finds this insufficient to avoid seeking protection.

propositions.text: Even if XXXXX is influential, influence limited to XXXXXXXX state where he lives
Claimant could have sought protection in XXXXXX, 1,700 km from XXXXX

paragraphs.summary: The court finds XXXXX's influence limited geographically and claimant could have sought protection elsewhere in Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation insufficient to explain why authorities were not approached before leaving
Claimant failed to exhaust all possible courses of action before seeking international protection

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects claimant's explanation and concludes he failed to exhaust all domestic protection options.

propositions.text: Claimant must show all reasonable steps taken to seek state protection and interaction with authorities

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimant must demonstrate reasonable efforts and interaction with authorities to seek protection.

propositions.text: Claimant is Mexican national; Mexico functions normally, not in complete breakdown
Country presumed capable of protection, claimant must seek protection before refugee claim
Documentary evidence shows Mexico has complaint mechanisms by phone, in person, online
No evidence claimant made serious effort or exhausted all courses to obtain state protection

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant is Mexican, Mexico functions normally with complaint mechanisms, but claimant made no serious effort to seek protection.

propositions.text: Claimant did not make serious effort or exhaust all courses to obtain state protection
Claimant failed to rebut presumption that Mexico can protect him

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed to seek protection and thus failed to rebut presumption of Mexican state protection.

propositions.text: To rebut presumption, claimant must provide clear and convincing evidence of state's inability to protect
Evidence must be reliable, probative, and satisfy balance of probabilities standard

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimant must provide clear, convincing, reliable evidence proving state protection is inadequate.

propositions.text: Claimant did not provide clear and convincing evidence Mexican state cannot or will not protect him

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant failed to prove Mexican state cannot or will not protect him.

propositions.text: Claimed discrimination due to sexual orientation including school mistreatment, family abuse, job instability

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges discrimination and persecution due to his homosexuality including abuse and job difficulties.

propositions.text: Panel accepts claimant is homosexual but finds discrimination allegations exaggerated

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts claimant's homosexuality but finds his discrimination claims exaggerated.

propositions.text: Claimant's school and work history as amended is not extraordinary

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's amended school and work history is not unusual.

propositions.text: Claimant gave inconsistent personal information in amendments versus initial forms
Claimant said he did not pay attention to discrepancies in personal information

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant gave inconsistent information; claimant says he did not pay attention.

propositions.text: Claimant's last-minute amendments to personal info were to harmonize narrative with homosexuality claim
Claimant's explanation for late amendments is unsatisfactory

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's late amendments were to align with his narrative and finds his explanation unsatisfactory.

propositions.text: Claimant did not mention sexual orientation as fear in initial forms
Claimant gave no satisfactory reason for omission of sexual orientation in initial fear explanation

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant omitted sexual orientation fear initially and gave no satisfactory explanation.

propositions.text: Alleged discrimination does not amount to persecution

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant's alleged discrimination does not constitute persecution.

propositions.text: Claimant has an internal flight alternative in Mexico

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant has an internal flight alternative within Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant was asked about fears if living elsewhere in Mexico such as La Paz or Mexico City

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant was asked about fears living in other Mexican cities.

propositions.text: Claimant testified XXXXX could find him anywhere in Mexico

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified that XXXXX could find him anywhere in Mexico.

propositions.text: The claimant submitted no reason why it would be unreasonable to seek refuge in one of these cities within the meaning of case law
The claimant submitted no real and concrete evidence of risk of persecution or risk to life or cruel and unusual treatment

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant gave no reason or evidence that seeking refuge elsewhere is unreasonable or that he faces persecution or risk.

propositions.text: Burden of proof for internal flight alternative rests on the claimant
Applicant must establish unreasonableness of seeking refuge elsewhere or conditions preventing relocation
Justice Lagacé stated this in Ramirez case

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Justice Lagacé in Ramirez that the claimant bears burden to prove unreasonableness of internal flight alternative or conditions preventing relocation.

propositions.text: Burden of proof on internal flight alternatives is on the applicant
Refugee claimant must show it would be unreasonable to seek refuge elsewhere
Justice Shore recalled this settled law in Palacios

paragraphs.summary: The court recalls Justice Shore in Palacios that the applicant must prove unreasonableness of seeking refuge elsewhere for internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Onus is on claimant to show serious risk of persecution in part of country with internal flight alternative on balance of probabilities
Court of Appeal established this in Thirunavukkarasu

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Court of Appeal in Thirunavukkarasu that claimant must prove serious risk of persecution in area with internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Claimant is 26 years old with 12 years education and 5 years labour market experience in Mexico

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant's age, education, and work experience in Mexico.

propositions.text: Panel does not believe the incidents allegedly occurred in 2008
Panel does not believe XXXXX still has interest in claimant given passage of time

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the panel disbelieved the 2008 incidents and that XXXXX no longer has interest in claimant due to time passed.

propositions.text: Claimant did not discharge burden of proof as set out in case law
Claimant has an internal flight alternative
Internal flight alternative alone is sufficient to dispose of refugee claim under section 96 or subsection 97(1) IRPA
Justice Shore stated this in Palacios

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed burden of proof and has internal flight alternative, which alone suffices to dispose refugee claim per Justice Shore in Palacios.

propositions.text: Claimant cannot succeed; fear has no objective basis under section 96 or 97 IRPA
Claimant can avail himself of state protection

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant cannot succeed as his fear lacks objective basis and he can access state protection.

propositions.text: Refugee protection claim is rejected

paragraphs.summary: The court orders rejection of the refugee protection claim.
